findings.text: blocking: retention_sweep is the pass the hourly reckon-crew-retention service runs (gc.main, gc.py:2142) and it never calls _sweep_worktree_trash; that sweep runs only from garbage_collect (gc.py:906), reached only by the crew gc CLI (crew_run_commands.py:2229). With no recurring crew gc on the fleet, every promotion now leaves a full worktree copy in the trash root permanently, so the done-when's 'removed by a recurring pass of a reckon service that already runs on the fleet' is unmet and the deliverable's 'never left behind indefinitely' is not satisfied by the landed code.

blocking: the head gate log the manifest names in test_logs ends at line 3 with its '# command:' header and carries no pytest summary and no bare EXIT= line, so the gate's status is unreadable from the record; the run that wrote it was killed after roughly six minutes (mtime 19:37:52Z against a 19:31:32Z start) and overwrote an earlier complete log, so the manifest's quoted '2 passed in 13.91s EXIT=0' cannot be checked against the file it cites.

non-blocking: assert isinstance(outcome.get('result'), object) is true for None and for every value, so it can never fail; the first promotion's exit code is never asserted (outcome['result'] is a CliRunner result that is discarded), so a first promotion that errored silently still passes this case.

non-blocking: the second case promotes the same run rather than 'another run' as the done-when words it, and promotion locks are per run (reckon/crew/runs.py:472, locks/<run_id>.lock), so two different runs never contend; the 31.1 s wait the negative control measures is of a scenario the live serial sweep cannot produce, which the manifest records under outside_scope (3).

non-blocking: the test backdates the copy's mtime by two hours before driving the sweep, implying an age gate, but _sweep_worktree_trash (reckon/crew/gc.py:126-133) removes every directory it finds regardless of age, so the assertion at :256-257 holds identically for a fresh copy and the done-when's 'no copy older than one hour survives it' is not what the line tests.

non-blocking: the done-when requires 'the existing tests of _read_pointer_or_rebuild pass unchanged', and this is the only test file naming that function, but no recorded log or stream command ran it, so that clause of the done-when is unevidenced; the change does not touch the pointer read, so the risk is in the record rather than the code.

item_verdicts.call_sites: verified the production callers of the changed release path: two promotion sites, promotion_release.py:462, the discard releases at routing.py:1694 and :2495, the gc releases at gc.py:834/:842/:856, and the sweep at gc.py:906.
item_verdicts.diff: read the single commit c203e0e247 against base d2e5fb667e: routing.py adds a ContextVar and its context manager and an early return before the deletion; promotion.py wraps the two _release_after_promotion calls; the new 303-line test file; the 24-line landing fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when asks a slowed promotion to return within 5 s of an undelayed one (tests/test_a_promotion_does_not_wait_for_its_worktree_copy_deletion.py:237), a second promotion to reach the lock within 5 s (:298), the copy to be removed by a recurring pass of a reckon service that already runs on the fleet, the _read_pointer_or_rebuild tests to pass unchanged, and both suite arms on all_debug; the first four are only partly met and the partition is not used, see the findings at reckon/crew/gc.py:1826 and gate-head.log:3.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that a promotion does not wait for its worktree copy's deletion; reckon/crew/routing.py:1516 leaves the moved-aside copy in the trash root when the deferring scope is set and reckon/crew/promotion.py:1357 and :2031 set it around both _release_after_promotion calls, so the wait is gone.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, commits c203e0e247, four changed_paths, tests the one-file pytest command, test_logs naming gate-head.log, negative-control-base.log and both suite arms, baseline_suite and after_suite both completed with the same single failure id, and an outside_scope block that honestly records the unwired recurring sweep.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the plan section and the orientation manifest declare reckon/crew/routing.py, reckon/crew/promotion.py, the evidence fragment directory, the figure directory and the new test file; git show --stat c203e0e247 lands exactly two modules, the new test and the fragment, with no figure, all inside that scope.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_promotion_does_not_wait_for_its_worktree_copy_deletion.py:237 asserts the slowed promotion returns within 5 s of the undelayed one and reddens at the base revision with 31.1 s, so it fails if the deferral is reverted; the second case's line 297 assertion is vacuous, which is why this is not higher.
justifications.evidence: The core measure is recorded and discriminating (negative-control-base.log ends "2 failed in 77.33s" EXIT=1 with the 31.1 s lock wait), but the file the manifest names as the head gate log holds no pytest summary and no EXIT= line, the sweep the done-when requires is not the sweep the hourly service runs, and the "existing tests of _read_pointer_or_rebuild pass unchanged" clause was never run.
justifications.fit: The new names describe the mechanism (deferring_worktree_copy_deletion, _DEFER_COPY_DELETION) with no plan, phase or ticket identifier, and the ContextVar idiom at reckon/crew/routing.py:1453 matches LAUNCH_RUN_ID at :1079 and ADMISSION_REVIEW_UNITS at :2653.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The goal sentence is met: reckon/crew/routing.py:1516 returns the release result before _delete_worktree_copy whenever _DEFER_COPY_DELETION is set, and reckon/crew/promotion.py:1357 and :2031 enter that scope around both _release_after_promotion calls, so a promotion no longer waits on the copy's deletion; the deliverable's second half is not met, see the finding at reckon/crew/gc.py:1826.
justifications.reuse: The change extends the owners in place rather than forking them: it reuses _release_worktree_whole (reckon/crew/routing.py:1473), the existing trash root and _sweep_worktree_trash (reckon/crew/gc.py:119), and a capability search over reckon/crew for another deferral or trash-sweep owner found none.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show c203e0e247 changes only reckon/crew/routing.py, reckon/crew/promotion.py, docs/evidence/fragments/a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline/a-promotion-does-not-wait-for-its-worktree-copy-s-deletion.html and the new tests/test_a_promotion_does_not_wait_for_its_worktree_copy_deletion.py, all inside the plan section's declared write paths, with the test file added because the plan names it though the dispatch's scope list omitted it.
